target_customer: Dental and orthodontic practices, paying for an AI front desk
problem: Dental front desks miss calls, fail to recall overdue patients and spend time on insurance verification, leaving chairs empty.
business_model: B2B SaaS per practice for AI voice and text patient engagement integrated with dental practice management software

founders.name: Adhira Tippur
founders.background_notes: YC page: grew up helping at her mother's dental practices; Rice University coverage describes her as a Rice student.

founders.name: Aditya Jain
education: Computer science and math, Georgia Tech

competitors.name: Weave (TrueLark AI Receptionist)
competitors.what: Phone and messaging platform with an AI receptionist after buying TrueLark

competitors.name: Peerlogic (Aimee)
competitors.what: Dental AI assistant for patient scheduling

competitors.name: Patientdesk AI
competitors.what: Y Combinator backed AI receptionist for dental calls and insurance

technical_complexity.rationale: Voice agents with integrations to Dentrix, Open Dental and other dental systems, plus insurance verification, require many integrations but use available speech and LLM components.

defensibility.rationale: Practice management integrations create some stickiness, but many funded dental AI receptionists sell the same features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Weave bought TrueLark in May 2025 and Planet DDS announced AI agents inside Denticon and Cloud9; incumbents were already shipping the wedge.

market_need_then: Weave reported in a 2026 survey that 47 percent of dental practices face staffing shortages; Kairos reports 16 live locations in October 2026 (Fondo blog) and early traction claims of 4x ARR growth since joining YC.

branding.name_origin: Kairos is an ancient Greek word for the right or opportune moment; no source states the founders chose it for that meaning.
branding.domain_note: Site kairoshealthai.com, so the plain domain was not used.

identity.logo: not described by any source found
identity.voice_and_tone: calm and caring, A little less administration. A lot more care.

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage from Rice University, Poets and Quants and an America250 startup list in July 2026; no merch or fan content.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is shared with many other Kairos companies, and the evidence of brand strength is limited to local university press.

outcome_analysis: Kairos Health is an active Fall 2026 company started by Rice and Georgia Tech students, one of whom grew up in her mother's dental practices, and it reports quick early growth. There is no exit. The main risk is that the dental AI receptionist market is crowded with funded startups and incumbents already bundling similar features.
notes: Funding: Rice Business and American Bazaar report about 70K in non-dilutive awards (about 22K from a Rice launch challenge), seen only in search snippets and not opened, so not recorded as a round. Caplight lists a 150K pre-seed led by Fusen Fund dated 2026-07-04, a single aggregator, unverified. Founded year not stated on the YC page. Founder roles are not stated, so Co-founder is used. Technical flag for Adhira Tippur is inferred from her consulting and venture background only and may be wrong. Completeness pass: the $150K pre-seed rests on a single database (Caplight). The grant entry is American Bazaar reporting more than $70,000 in non-dilutive funding to date (about $22K from Rice competitions), a single outlet, no date.
